name: rbind.zoo
title: Merge Two or More zoo Objects

arguments.text: Zoo series to stack. NULL arguments are dropped.

arguments.name: deparse.level
arguments.text: Accepted and ignored. The installed body does not use it.

origin.details: Indexes are concatenated and then sorted by the zoo constructor. An index that appears twice is an error. Every series must have the same number of columns. When the column names are a permutation of the first series, those columns are reordered. Otherwise a warning is issued and the physical order is kept. Vectors stay vectors. A mix of a vector and a one-column matrix follows the shape of the first series.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(c(1, 2), c(1, 2))
y <- zoo(c(3, 4), c(4, 5))
z <- rbind(x, y)
show <- function(v) paste(vapply(as.numeric(v), function(a) if (is.na(a)) "NA" else sprintf("%.16g", a), ""), collapse = " ")
cat(show(coredata(z)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(show(index(z)), "\n", sep = "")

arguments.name: *args
arguments.text: Zoo series to stack. None is dropped.

arguments.name: deparse_level
arguments.text: Accepted and ignored, as in the installed R body.

translation.details: Indexes are concatenated and sorted with the values. An index that appears twice is an error. Every series must have the same number of columns. When the column names are a permutation of the first series, those columns are reordered. A matrix is Fortran order.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.merge import rbind_zoo

def show(values):
    array = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    flat = array.reshape(-1, order="F") if array.ndim == 2 else array.reshape(-1)
    parts = []
    for value in flat:
        value = float(value)
        parts.append("NA" if math.isnan(value) else format(value, ".16g"))
    return " ".join(parts)

x = Zoo([1.0, 2.0], [1.0, 2.0])
y = Zoo([3.0, 4.0], [4.0, 5.0])
z = rbind_zoo(x, y)
print(show(z.data))
print(show(z.index))
